subject.title: Feature Request: Add cumulative history search and multi-account support

question: Should Wacrawl evolve from a single replace-current-archive model into a persistent multi-profile cumulative archive, and which part should be designed first?
rationale: The request changes archive identity, retention, deduplication, restore, and backup semantics; source inspection cannot determine the intended permanent product contract or compatibility policy.

options.title: Design cumulative retention first
options.body: Split the request and first specify account-scoped stable identities, cumulative upserts, deletion semantics, migration, and historical search before adding named profile UX.

options.title: Implement snapshot federation
options.body: Keep current archives immutable and add search across selected historical snapshots, accepting additional checkout, decryption, and query complexity.

options.title: Keep point-in-time archives
options.body: Retain the existing replacement and restore model and document separate `--db` archives as the supported manual account-isolation workflow.

recommendation.title: Design cumulative retention first
recommendation.body: Split the request and first specify account-scoped stable identities, cumulative upserts, deletion semantics, migration, and historical search before adding named profile UX.

likelyOwner.reason: The current backup and historical-restore contract appears to originate primarily from this person's merged work.
